## What our people are saying

### Hermes

Same event everywhere you look — 4 outlets, 4 different ways in. Here's how each one leads it: Bloomberg.com opens with "New Trump Tariffs Won’t Top Trade Deal Levels, Will Be Targeted"; TradingView opens with "Market Sources: U.S. Tariffs Expected Tuesday Will Not Exceed Trade Deal Limits"; Forex Factory opens with "New US Tariffs Expected Tuesday Won't Exceed Trade Deal Levels; Tariffs To Be Targeted, Not Blanket Rate, Pers"; marketscreener.com opens with "New US Tariffs Won't Top Levels Set in Trade Deals".

Every version landed on my desk, and laid out side by side, they can't even agree on what the story is. Bloomberg.com wants you thinking about "New Trump Tariffs Won’t Top Trade Deal Levels, Will Be Targeted". TradingView wants you thinking about "Market Sources: U.S. Tariffs Expected Tuesday Will Not Exceed Trade Deal Limits". Forex Factory wants you thinking about "New US Tariffs Expected Tuesday Won't Exceed Trade Deal Levels; Tariffs To Be Targeted, No". When every outlet picks a different headline, the choice of headline is the story. Read one and you will feel informed. Read them all and you will realize each one buried somebody else's lead.

Bloomberg.com leads with "New Trump Tariffs Won’t Top Trade Deal Levels, Will Be Targeted". TradingView leads with "Market Sources: U.S. Tariffs Expected Tuesday Will Not Exceed Trade Deal Limits". Same event. Read those two lines back to back and tell me they are the same story. They are not two doors into one room. They are two different rooms, and somebody built them that way. If you read only one of them this morning, somebody chose your opinion for you, and it was not you. I am not saying any one telling is false. I am saying no single telling is the whole event, and the gap between them is where you were played.

### Dionysus
